issues.detail: The Greek 'ποιησαι ενα προσηλυτον' (to make someone a proselyte) is translated as 'làm cho một người trở thành người mới theo đạo' (to make someone a new person in the faith). While 'proselyte' implies conversion, the Vietnamese rendering 'người mới theo đạo' adds a nuance of 'newness' not present in the specific term 'proselytos'.

The Greek 'διπλοτερον υμων' (twice as much as you/doubly your [sin]) is rendered as 'gấp đôi các ngươi' (double you). The Vietnamese phrasing lacks the sense of 'doubly' referring to the magnitude of the sin/offense, making it sound like a numerical doubling of the people themselves.
